doc.title: Milt Fillius interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 18, 2000

title: Meeting Nikki again after decades
summary: He met Nelma Chauncy ('Nikki') in eighth grade, reconnected years later after her husband's death, and married her.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: That’s funny. Well let me ask you about what has to be one of the great things in this part of your life and that is Nikki.
There’s an interesting story about the longevity of how long you two actually knew each other.

It was quite a while but we don’t like to add up the years really. We first met in the eighth grade at John Marshall High School in Rochester, New York. And we have known of each other since. We came apart after college, when I went to college and she went to college. We met again in Buffalo when I went up to sign up in the Navy, enlist in the Navy, that’s another story. And I ran into her and we knew each other, and we’d have gotten married then but she didn’t return my phone call. Anyway, so it went on and then a few years ago I was in Rochester visiting my sister, and with my old friend whom you’ve met, Bob Steamer who had the band with me. We were at a place and a guy came and says, “By the way, Nelma Chauncy — which is Nikki’s real name — lives on my street and she’s a widow and she does a lot of gardening” and so on and so forth. So on the way back I said to my friend I said I’m really curious about Nelma, I haven’t seen her in years, get her address for me so I can write her a note. So I did and she did and there you go. She bewitched me. But she’s the best thing that ever happened to me. She’s been a wonderful — she’s gotten into jazz right up to here. She has befriended and been befriended by all my jazz friends and she’s just a hell of a woman. Right? NF: You got that right.
